item.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
item.description:
Image source, ReutersByOlivia Ireland and Bethany Bell, Reporting fromViennaPublished16 November 2026, 11:17 GMTUpdated 1 hour ago
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.
Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.
The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.
Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.
The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.
Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".
The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.
The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.
In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.
In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

item.title: Yemeni forces retreat to defend port city from Houthis
item.description:
Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Pro-government forces said troops were being moved to defend the interim capital, Aden (file photo)ByKaty Watson, Reporting fromJerusalem and Olivia IrelandPublished16 November 2026, 03:08 GMTUpdated 6 hours ago
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they are redeploying troops to defend the country's interim capital, Aden, following weeks of intensified fighting with the Iran-backed Houthi movement.
The Southern Armed Forces said it was withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea, to reinforce positions around Aden and neighbouring areas.
Houthi-run media say the movement has taken control of the evacuated territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the key shipping route which the Houthis seized in a surprise offensive in September.
Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis. The Iran-backed fighters said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior.
But the Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority".
It said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area" with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats".
"This step is driven by the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates, reinforcing the front lines and addressing existing threats."

item.title: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Donald Trump greeting Jensen Huang in September this yearByMichael RaceBusiness reporterPublished16 November 2026, 11:45 GMTUpdated 42 minutes ago
US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated.
Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.
It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.
But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back".
The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.
President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.
"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.
The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive.
They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".
Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.
However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

item.title: Man sentenced over 'horrific' attempted murder of three children
item.description:
Image source, PA MediaImage caption,
In July Riad Bouchaker was found guilty of the eight charges he facedByClaire Graham and Daniel Logan, BBC News NIPublished16 November 2026, 11:34 GMTUpdated 5 hours ago
A 52-year-old man has been sentenced to life in prison for the attempted murder of three children outside a primary school in Dublin's Parnell Square in November 2023.
Riad Bouchaker, of no fixed address, was also found guilty of assault causing serious harm to creche worker Leanne Flynn, and of assaulting two other children and a teenager.
On Monday, Judge Tony Hunt imposed the overall sentence of life imprisonment in Dublin's Central Criminal Court.
Rioting across many parts of Dublin following the attack led to the deployment of the most riot police in Irish history.
Bouchaker was originally from Algeria but had lived in Ireland for 25 years prior to the attack, and he had Irish citizenship.
He was assisted by an Arabic interpreter and a speech-and-language expert during the trial, who were present in court for the sentencing.
Image source, PA MediaImage caption,
The attack took place outside a primary school on Parnell Square East
The attack took place outside Gaelscoil Choláiste Mhuire in Parnell Square, shortly after 13:40 local time on 23 November.
A group of 13 children, aged five and six, were lined up on Parnell Square waiting to go to their afterschool provision. Childcare worker Leanne Flynn was helping a little boy zip up his jacket when Bouchaker pulled his knife on the children.
A five-year-old girl was left with a lifelong brain injury after being stabbed in the heart.
Now eight, she is non-verbal and can only communicate by blinking, uses a wheelchair and has to be fed through a tube in her stomach as she cannot swallow safely by herself.
The judge said the child will never live independently and that her life, and the lives of her family, had been permanently altered.

item.title: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Raye's latest record This Album May Contain Hope also won the Mercury Prize last monthBySteven McIntoshEntertainment reporter Published3 hours ago
British singer Raye leads the charge at the forthcoming Grammy Awards with 11 nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumous nods.
Raye is nominated for her latest Mercury-winning record This Album May Contain Hope and its lead single Where Is My Husband!, which is up for both song and record of the year.
Other nominees include Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Dean, Ariana Grande, Bruno Mars, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Miranda Lambert and Phoebe Bridgers.
Parton's two nominations, both in the best country duo/group performance category, come three months after the country music star died aged 80.
Parton is recognised for Butterfly, her collaboration with the Zac Brown Band, and Light of a Clear Blue Morning, alongside an all-star line-up including her goddaughter Miley Cyrus.
The late country star also received a nomination for best audio book, for her narration of Star of the Show: My Life on Stage.
The Grammy Awards 2027 will take place on Sunday 7 February in Los Angeles.

Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Dolly Parton scored two nominations, three months after her death aged 80
Madonna's album Confessions II, a sequel to 2005's Confessions on a Dancefloor, was absent from the "big four" categories - including album, record and song of the year.
That will be seen by many as the Grammys continuing their tradition of snubbing the US singer, but the album did make it into the best dance category.
Rosalía's nine nominations for her widely acclaimed album Lux come after her huge success at last week's Latin Grammy Awards.

item.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
item.description:
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
The Kerch bridge was built in 2018 and is one of President Putin's signature infrastructure projects (file photo)ByLaura GozziPublished2 hours ago
Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.
The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.
Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.
The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war.
The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.
The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.
Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment.

item.title: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza
item.description:
Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
A heavy storm earlier this month damaged tents and caused widespread floodingByYolande Knell, Middle East correspondent, Reporting fromJerusalem and Victoria BournePublished8 hours ago
The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire".
The foreign ministers warn recent floods have brought "further suffering" to the war-torn territory, which recently had its first winter storm.
The statement says 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border.
The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory.
It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".
The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs said the widespread flooding and a landslide led to a number of deaths, thousands of damaged shelters and the suspension of critical services.
The statement from the British, Australian, Canadian and Italian foreign ministers says, external: "This situation is entirely reversible - and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in."
"The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in. Dual-use items necessary for humanitarian operations and early recovery must be granted entry before it is too late."
The European Union issued a similar statement on Saturday, external, reiterating its "grave concern" over what it called the "persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis".
The EU also urged Israel to comply with international law.
The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

item.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
item.description:
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
Gérard Depardieu appeared at a courthouse in Paris on Monday for his appeal trial that was due to startByHugh SchofieldParis correspondentPublished4 hours ago
French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault, admitting that his behaviour towards women had often been offensive and offering a "deep and sincere" apology.
On the day that the appeal was due to start in a Paris court, the 77-year-old actor's unexpected mea culpa marks a dramatic reversal of his previous denials of sexual impropriety.
"Justice was pronounced. I was found guilty. I understand and bow to this conviction… I have therefore decided to abandon the appeal," he wrote.
It means he is now guilty in law of abusing two women during a film shoot in Paris five years ago, and his 18-month suspended prison term stands.
"Victory is ours, and we welcome it with head held high," said one of the two women, named only as Amélie, who was at the court.
"There is huge relief because the fight is over. The giant of film has fallen," said the other woman in the case, who is known in court by the false name Sarah.
In his statement, Depardieu appeared to have undergone a major shift from his earlier stance of unapologetic intransigence.
"For a long time on film shoots I hid myself behind provocation and smut. I thought that the remarks I made, and certain gestures that I made, were of no consequence.
"I see now that there is a border between impertinence and offence. Never, ever did I intend to hurt the women with whom I came into contact. But I see now that intention has no bearing on the hurt that people feel.
"Cases before the courts are damaging. Everything got out of hand… including my defence. Many people have suffered in this story. I have not the power to go back in time. I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that has disappeared."

item.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
item.description:
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
The Estonian government says it will shut the crossings after accusing Russia of directing an alleged sabotage attack on a drone manufacturer ByPhoebe HopsonPublished3 hours ago
Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe".
The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian.
They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids.
On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries.
The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website.
Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia".
Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage.
The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media.
Estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with Russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions.
One of them is located at Narva, Estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border.

item.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Gun violence remains a persistent problem in South Africa, where about 60 people are murdered every day, according to police (file photo)ByOndiro OgangaPublished6 hours ago
South African police are investigating the murders of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night.
Eight men were fatally shot in a minibus in KwaZulu-Natal province. Police declared them dead when they arrived at the scene. Hours later, nine people were found shot dead inside a shack in western Pretoria.
Police say the two incidents are unrelated. The motive for the shootings has not yet been established.
South Africa is struggling to contain violent crime, including gang-related killings. The country has one of the world's highest murder rates.
Police say they responded to reports of a shooting ⁠outside Pietermaritzburg town in KwaZulu-Natal and found a white seven-seater vehicle riddled with bullet holes.
Inside were eight men with multiple gunshot wounds.
"It has not been established how the incident happened, and police are collecting pieces of evidence to determine the possible motive of the killings and the identity of the suspects," police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said.
The police have launched a manhunt for the suspects.
In a separate shooting in the Jeffsville informal settlement in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, police found the bodies of six men and three women.
They are believed to have been killed inside a four-room shack between 22:00 and 23:00 on Sunday. The bodies were scattered across the rooms, with several spent cartridges discovered outside the shack.
Community members initially mistook the gunshots for thunder and lightning.
